checkpoints.question: What is the primary security benefit of using a jump server for administrator access?

options.A: It automatically encrypts all traffic between the admin workstation and the internal servers
options.B: It creates a single authorized gateway through which all admin traffic is funneled to protected systems
options.C: It prevents administrators from needing to remember passwords for any of the internal systems
options.D: It eliminates the need for administrators to use multi-factor authentication on their own workstations

checkpoints.explanation: A jump server acts as the single authorized gateway through which all administrator traffic must pass, reducing attack surface by centralizing access control. The other options misrepresent jump server functionality or confuse it with related technologies like MFA or encryption.

checkpoints.question: Which load balancer layer can decrypt HTTPS traffic from clients and inspect request headers and URL paths before forwarding?

options.A: Layer 4 load balancer using least-connections algorithm with health checks
options.B: Layer 7 load balancer using round-robin distribution and weighted routing
options.C: Layer 7 load balancer using SSL termination and HTTP-aware routing
options.D: Layer 4 load balancer using IP hash routing with session persistence

checkpoints.explanation: Only Layer 7 load balancers operate at the application layer and can perform SSL termination to decrypt HTTPS and inspect HTTP headers and URL paths. Layer 4 operates only at the transport layer and cannot perform these functions.

checkpoints.question: What is the key difference between a forward proxy and a reverse proxy in terms of where each sits and whom it serves?

options.A: A forward proxy sits on the server side and protects backend servers from external threats and attacks
options.B: A forward proxy requires explicit client configuration to function, while a reverse proxy requires firewall rules to function
options.C: A forward proxy performs SSL/TLS inspection on traffic, while a reverse proxy performs load distribution and caching
options.D: A forward proxy sits on the client side and serves internal users, while a reverse proxy sits on the server side and protects backend servers

checkpoints.explanation: A forward proxy sits between internal clients and the internet to serve those clients; a reverse proxy sits between internet clients and backend servers to protect those servers. The positioning and direction of service is the fundamental distinction between them.

checkpoints.question: In a negative security model WAF, what is the core limitation when defending against novel application-layer attacks?

options.A: It requires constant signature updates and cannot detect previously unknown attack patterns
options.B: It is complex to configure because it must define every valid input format and request pattern
options.C: It blocks legitimate requests that do not match known attack signatures in its database
options.D: It decrypts HTTPS traffic at the gateway, which adds latency to all client requests

checkpoints.explanation: The negative security model maintains a list of known-bad patterns and blocks matches, so novel attacks not yet in the signature database can bypass it. A positive model has the opposite weakness: it is complex to configure, which is why the negative model was described with that limitation.
